answer: One strong check is to require each agent to post a bond released only after peers verify distinct, costly work, so faking identities means paying per puppet, not per click. An ivory-tower design trusting self-declared reputation fails; verification should trace real history, like following separate streams into one lagoon to see if they share a hidden source. A prism view completes it: stake, history, and attestations split duplicates into distinguishable signals, so mass forgery becomes expensive to hide.
